title: Free Time
description: What you do for fun: going out, films, music, sport and the weekend.

items.english: to go out, go for a walk; to travel around
items.registerNotes: Anything from a stroll to a holiday trip. Jalan-jalan saja (just out and about) is the classic answer to Mau ke mana?

items.english: to watch (a film, TV, a match)
items.registerNotes: What everyone says: nonton film, nonton TV. Menonton is the written form.
The cinema is bioskop: nonton di bioskop.

items.cultureNote: Dangdut, a pop style with Malay and Indian roots, is what you'll hear on buses, at weddings and from passing street musicians.

items.registerNotes: To sing is nyanyi, written menyanyi. Karaoke with friends is a favourite night out.

items.english: to play; to come over, visit
items.registerNotes: Main ke rumah, ya (come round to my place) uses main for visiting. Written bermain.
Also a verb: Saya olahraga setiap pagi (I exercise every morning). Football is sepak bola, usually just bola: nonton bola.
A swimming pool is a kolam renang. In casual speech, renang on its own: Ayo renang.
Ask before photographing someone: Boleh foto?
items.cultureNote: At tourist spots, people may ask a foreigner for a photo together (foto bareng).

items.registerNotes: Liburan ke Bali is a holiday in Bali; Saya di sini untuk liburan (I'm here on holiday). Libur on its own is a day off.
Casual: hanging out with friends, often for hours at a warung kopi or café. To someone older, say kumpul dengan teman (meeting up with friends).
The everyday form: Saya suka baca. Written membaca.
Hobinya apa? (What are your hobbies?) is a common getting-to-know-you question.

items.pitfallNote: Malam Minggu, literally Sunday night, is Saturday night: the eve of Sunday, and the night for going out.
